In standard physics-informed neural networks, initial and terminal states are enforced through additional weighted loss terms, resulting in a multi-objective optimization problem that is highly sensitive to the choice of loss weights and can lead to poor convergence and reduced accuracy. To address this challenge, we construct a simple transformation, exploiting the mathematical structure of trajectory optimization problems, to enforce boundary conditions exactly a-priori. This transformation can be interpreted as a reparameterization of the solution space that embeds the boundary conditions directly into the function. This converts the original constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one over admissible trajectories. I.e. the transformation eliminates the boundary condition penalty terms and reduces the problem to a single-objective optimization. Crucially, trajectory optimization comes with a low-dimensional boundary, which allows particularly simple and stable constructions of distance functions compared to general domains in partial differential equations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach meaningfully improves convergence behavior and solution accuracy.
items.title_ko: 정확한 경계 조건을 갖는 우주선 궤적 최적화를 위한 물리정보 신경망
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 물리정보 신경망(PINN)을 사용하여 우주선 궤적을 최적화하는 새로운 방법을 제시합니다. 기존 PINN이 초기 및 최종 상태를 손실 항으로만 처리하여 민감도가 높았던 문제를 개선, 정확한 경계 조건을 직접 반영함으로써 신경망 파라미터에 대한 추력 최소화를 통해 궤적을 최적화하는 데 성공했습니다.
items.why_ko: 우주선 궤적 최적화와 같은 고전적인 공학 문제를 AI 기반으로 효율적이고 정확하게 해결할 수 있는 방법을 제시하여, 실제 우주 탐사 및 위성 운영 분야에 활용 가능성이 큽니다.

items.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
items.body: This study proposes an interesting approach for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, which integrates blockchain technology, federated learning (FL), and allocation optimization of latency and resources. The research evaluates the proposed system using various performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), model accuracy, and latency and demonstrates its superiority over existing techniques. Furthermore, the system provides enhanced security through consensus optimization and k-anonymity for data privacy. Overall, the proposed system is a promising solution for efficient and secure V2V communication in the era of connected and autonomous vehicles. Moreover, the proposed approach achieves higher reliability, lower latency, and better resource utilization compared to traditional 5G.
items.title_ko: 블록체인 기반 6G 기술과 연합 학습을 활용한 V2V 통신
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 블록체인 기술, 연합 학습(FL), 그리고 지연 시간 및 자원 할당 최적화를 통합한 혁신적인 V2V(차량 간 통신) 접근 방식을 제안합니다. 패킷 전달률, 모델 정확도, 지연 시간 등 다양한 성능 지표를 통해 기존 기술 대비 우수성을 입증하며, 합의 최적화와 k-익명성을 통해 보안을 강화합니다.
items.why_ko: 미래 자율주행 및 스마트 교통 시스템의 핵심인 V2V 통신의 효율성과 보안을 획기적으로 개선할 수 있는 통합 기술 솔루션을 제시합니다.

items.title: Polylogarithmic Regret via Certainty Equivalence in Degenerate LQR
items.body: Singular input penalties, as in minimum variance control, can reduce what must be identified to control an unknown linear system. In online linear quadratic control, certainty equivalence can achieve polylogarithmic regret when the optimal controller is identifiable from data collected under optimal feedback. With a positive definite input penalty, however, this condition is restrictive, since for an invertible state matrix it requires all unknown parameters to be identifiable under optimal feedback. We show that singular input penalties relax this requirement, expanding the class of problems in which certainty equivalence achieves polylogarithmic regret. Specifically, we prove that a certainty-equivalence algorithm with a short initial exploration phase achieves $O(\log^2 T)$ expected regret over $T$ interactions whenever controller identifiability holds. We complement this guarantee with an $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ minimax lower bound for a family containing a system where controller identifiability fails. For minimum variance control, knowing the range of the input matrix suffices for controller identifiability, a weaker requirement than knowing the full input matrix, as assumed in prior work with positive definite input penalties. This condition also covers underactuated systems, as we illustrate with a cart-pole example.
items.title_ko: 특이 LQR에서 확실성 등가 원리를 통한 다항 로그적 회귀
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 최소 분산 제어와 같이 특이 입력 페널티가 있는 경우, 불확실한 선형 시스템 제어에 필요한 식별 대상을 줄일 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 최적 제어기 아래에서 수집된 데이터로부터 최적 제어기를 식별할 수 있을 때, 온라인 선형 이차 제어에서 확실성 등가 원리가 다항 로그적 회귀를 달성할 수 있음을 입증합니다.
items.why_ko: 제어 이론 분야의 심층적인 연구로, 특정 조건에서 학습된 제어기의 성능 한계를 이론적으로 분석하여 관련 분야 연구자들에게 유의미한 정보를 제공합니다.

items.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
items.body: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. To address these issues, we propose Mixture-of-Features Attention (MoFA), a lightweight feature-encoding approach equipped with a working memory that encodes previously rejected proposals. Leveraging MoFA, rejection memory, and a set of further enhancements, including 2-tap causal convolutions, prefix-only cross-attention, and non-uniform target layer selection, the final architecture, DNeo, achieves 1.3x faster generation speed than SoTA (DFlash-2) without impacting drafter footprint or generation quality. DNeo marks a new state of the art in high quality, fast LLM inference.
items.title_ko: DNeo: 병렬 드래프트 모델을 위한 개선된 타겟 피처 인코딩
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 추론 속도를 높이는 스페큘레이티브 디코딩에서 병렬 드래프트 모델의 성능을 향상시키기 위해 '더 나은 타겟 피처 인코딩'의 중요성을 강조합니다. 기존 DFlash, DSpark와 같은 아키텍처가 타겟 모델이 계산한 풍부한 피처를 활용하여 드래프트 품질을 개선했지만, 표준 피처 인코딩 메커니즘의 한계를 지적하며 새로운 개선 방향을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 속도를 높이는 중요한 기술인 스페큘레이티브 디코딩의 효율성을 더욱 개선할 수 있는 핵심적인 방법을 제안하여, 대규모 모델의 실용성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy
items.body: Published face-privacy methods report protection above 90% against black-box recognition models. That number comes from an evaluation protocol with two independent defects, reported in a measure that cannot size either one. The input is wrong: methods published since 2022 feed the network the whole photograph, or a detector's box, where deployed systems detect, align to a landmark template and crop. Re-scoring the same files through a realistic front end costs a standard transfer attack 56% of its dodging protection and a budget-allocating attack 7%, with no image regenerated. The measure is wrong: that loss is a difference of success rates, so it saturates, moving by 8.2x over a budget sweep while the effect beneath it moves by 1.34x. We therefore report the paired cosine shift, in which both thresholds cancel algebraically, so the input defect holds without committing to a calibration. Measured that way it is 2.2x and 10.7x larger on three unseen recognizers, and at matched budget it reverses the L-infinity transfer ranking: the one surveyed method that aligns at evaluation gains 0.18 where MI-FGSM loses 0.05. The cause is a resampling mismatch, not perturbation lost outside the crop; optimising through a differentiable alignment operator largely removes it, adding +24 to +58 points on unseen recognizers and a commercial system, with a residual on one of them. The thresholds are wrong: the four constants inherited since 2021 hold the false-accept rate near its nominal 1% on aligned crops but admit 2.3-5.4% on whole images, with an opposite-signed bias across dodging and impersonation, the two tasks reported side by side. Differentiable alignment and gallery scoring are not new: the first generation of this literature used both, and we show what dropping them cost.
items.title_ko: 잘못된 입력, 잘못된 임계값: 적대적 얼굴 프라이버시 재평가
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 기존 얼굴 프라이버시 보호 방법들이 블랙박스 얼굴 인식 모델에 대해 90% 이상의 보호율을 보고하지만, 이는 평가 프로토콜의 결함 때문이라고 주장합니다. 특히, 실제 시스템과 달리 전면 사진이나 탐지기 박스를 입력으로 사용하고, 임계값 설정에 문제가 있음을 지적하며 현실적인 프런트 엔드를 통한 재평가를 강조합니다.
items.why_ko: 기존 AI 프라이버시 보호 기술의 실제 효과에 대한 근본적인 의문을 제기하며, 보다 현실적인 평가 방법을 통해 적절한 보안 수준을 확보하도록 개발자에게 경각심을 줍니다.

items.title: Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training
items.body: Controlled studies of latent two-hop reasoning train transformers to predict only the answer, whereas language models are trained to predict every token. We ask whether a model trained on every token learns to answer two-hop questions whose intermediate entity appears in no two-hop training example. We build a synthetic corpus with such questions. On this corpus every term of the loss can be computed exactly. A looped transformer, a standard transformer and DiscoLoop answer almost none of these questions. We therefore introduce the Baton family of looped transformers. They pass the intermediate entity to the second loop as a token embedding. When trained to predict only the answer, two of its three variants answer these questions almost perfectly. We then relate the success and failure of each model to three design conditions. Experiments that change one condition at a time agree with this hypothesis. When Baton is trained on every token, however, its accuracy on these questions rises and then declines. We further split the gradient of the next-token loss into three terms. Removing the two terms that depend on the particular training set raises the peak accuracy but does not remove the decline. The decline arises in the second hop while the model still recalls both facts.
items.title_ko: 다음 토큰 예측 학습 하에서의 잠재 사실 합성 능력
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 언어 모델이 '모든 토큰 예측' 방식으로 학습될 때, 중간 개체가 훈련 예시에 나타나지 않는 두 단계 추론 질문에 답할 수 있는 '잠재 사실 합성' 능력을 학습하는지 탐구합니다. 이를 위해 특정 유형의 질문에 대한 손실을 정확히 계산할 수 있는 합성 코퍼스를 구축하여 다양한 트랜스포머 모델의 성능을 평가합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 능력과 지식 합성 메커니즘을 심층적으로 이해하려는 연구로, 모델이 어떻게 새로운 정보를 조합하여 문제를 해결하는지 밝히는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: KVUse: Reusable-KV User Memory for Efficient LLM Recommenders
items.body: Memory-augmented recommenders built on large language models (LLMs) maintain a natural-language profile of each user. These profiles are updated by a user profile update path that revises the profile as new interactions arrive and are consumed by downstream task paths like ranking. Because these user profiles are stored as text in the user memory, every ranking LLM call that consumes them must splice them in the prompt and calculate the KV cache of them during the prefill phase. Given these ranking LLM calls are prefill heavy (long prompt but short decoded output) and repeatedly called, these repeated prefill of user profile text dominates the serving. Prefix caching cannot remove it, because these user profiles are preceded by different text in different calls. We present KVUse, which stores the user profiles as reusable key-value (KV) caches instead of text. KVUse trains lightweight LoRA writers by self-distillation, so that the user profile update call produces the reusable KV of the user profile while decoding it, and the LLM can read these reusable KV at new positions and behind new context without recomputation. KVUse also has a customized KV scheduler that uploads the stored reusable KV of the next batch while the current batch is computed, hiding the KV transfer from host memory behind GPU computation. On four InstructRec datasets with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, KVUse shows no statistically significant difference in ranking quality from full prefill over continuous memory update rounds. Under saturated load, KVUse raises the throughput of the downstream scoring path by 4.0x-4.5x and of the profile update path by 1.4x-1.9x.
items.title_ko: KVUse: 효율적인 LLM 추천기를 위한 재사용 가능한 KV 캐시 사용자 메모리
items.summary_ko: LLM 기반 추천 시스템에서 사용자 프로필이 텍스트 형태로 저장되고 매번 KV 캐시를 계산해야 하는 비효율성을 개선하기 위해 'KVUse'를 제안합니다. KVUse는 사용자 프로필의 KV 캐시를 재사용 가능한 형태로 저장하여, 랭킹 LLM 호출 시 프리필 단계를 최적화하고 메모리 및 컴퓨팅 비용을 절감합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 기반 추천 시스템의 메모리 사용량과 추론 비용을 획기적으로 줄일 수 있는 실용적인 최적화 기술로, 대규모 사용자 데이터를 다루는 서비스 개발자에게 매우 유용합니다.

items.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
items.body: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking. Given 50 demonstrations for each task, ALOHA Lightning autonomously completes bimanual tasks such as ball tossing and catching, folding shorts, battery insertion, and bussing tables for over 80% success rates while close to human speed. Project website: https://flash-aloha.github.io/
items.body_ko: 인간 시연을 통한 학습은 로봇이 다양한 조작 기술을 습득할 수 있도록 해주었지만, 학습된 정책은 일반적으로 일반적인 인간보다 훨씬 느리게 실행됩니다. 이러한 속도 차이는 주로 고속으로 시연 데이터를 수집하는 인터페이스의 부족과 고속 동작을 강력하게 실행할 수 있는 정책을 훈련하기 어렵기 때문입니다. 본 논문에서는 빠르고 정밀한 로봇 조작을 학습하기 위한 시스템인 ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA)을 제시합니다. 우리 시스템은 키네스테틱 티칭(kinesthetic teaching)을 사용하여 되돌림 가능한 양손 플랫폼에서 인간에 가까운 속도의 시연을 직관적으로 수집하여 자연스럽고 빠른 궤적을 생성합니다. 또한 테스트 시간 동작 스무딩(test-time action smoothing)을 통해 부드러운 고속 실행을 가능하게 하고 마스킹을 통해 데이터 수집과 배포 간의 시각 데이터 분포를 정렬하는 학습 파이프라인을 제시합니다. 각 작업에 대해 50개의 시연이 주어졌을 때, ALOHA Lightning은 공 던지기 및 잡기, 반바지 접기, 배터리 삽입, 테이블 정리와 같은 양손 작업을 80% 이상의 성공률로 인간 속도에 가깝게 자율적으로 완료합니다. 프로젝트 웹사이트: https://flash-aloha.github.io/
items.title_ko: ALOHA Lightning: 빠르고 정밀한 로봇 조작 학습 시스템
items.summary_ko: ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA)은 인간 시연을 통해 로봇이 빠르고 정밀한 조작 기술을 학습하도록 돕는 시스템입니다. 고속 시연 데이터 수집 인터페이스와 고속 동작을 안정적으로 실행할 수 있는 정책 훈련의 어려움을 해결하여, 기존 모방 학습 로봇의 실행 속도 한계를 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 인간처럼 빠르고 능숙하게 작업할 수 있도록 하는 핵심 기술로, 로봇의 실용성과 산업 적용 가능성을 크게 높이는 데 기여합니다. 실제 로봇 개발자들에게 매우 중요한 진전입니다.

items.title: Lost in a Few Heads: Diagnosing and Repairing Block Selection in Sparse Attention
items.body: Sparse attention models read a few blocks of keys for every query at a fixed budget and can lose much of their long-context retrieval accuracy at that budget. We ask where this loss is made. Using exact attention mass selection at the shipped budget as an oracle, we show that the selector under-ranks the needle rather than running out of budget. We find attention heads that miss the needle by running a calibration probe that teacher-forces the answer and reads two quantities in every head. The first is the needle attention that the selector forfeits, and the second is the share of the answer's log-probability that fixing the head's selection restores, integrated along the path from the shipped selector to full attention. Four checkpoints of the InfLLM-V2 family and NOSA-8B lose multi-key retrieval in the same three blind heads, which attend to the needle while a mean-pooled key summary dilutes its single decisive token. Full attention in those heads or a 4-bit scorer that keeps the shipped budget recovers most of the loss without training. On MiniCPM4.1-8B at 64K, either fix lifts multi-key retrieval accuracy from 54.1 to 97.5%, level with full attention in every head. In production serving engines, full attention in those heads keeps 84 to 89% of the time to first token (TTFT) that sparse attention saves at 32K to 128K context length. Beyond the InfLLM-V2 selector lineage, one unified rule flags attention heads above a threshold swept on each checkpoint until they close most of the gap to full attention on calibration prompts. A similar small set of blind attention heads carry the loss for the SeerAttention-R gates, NSA, and DashAttention, whereas many such heads exist in MoBA. On Qwen3-8B with the SeerAttention-R gates, full attention in 18 of 288 key-value heads lifts multi-key retrieval accuracy from 29.8 to 97.7%.
items.title_ko: 몇몇 헤드에서 길을 잃다: 스파스 어텐션의 블록 선택 진단 및 개선
items.summary_ko: 스파스 어텐션 모델이 고정된 예산 내에서 장문 컨텍스트 검색 정확도가 떨어지는 원인을 분석합니다. 선택기가 중요한 정보를 놓치는 것이 예산 부족 때문이 아니라 '니들(needle)'을 과소평가하기 때문임을 보여줍니다. '교정 프로브'를 사용하여 어떤 어텐션 헤드가 니들을 놓치는지 진단하고 개선 방향을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 핵심 구성 요소인 스파스 어텐션의 효율성과 정확도를 저해하는 근본적인 문제를 파악하고 개선하는 방법을 제시하여, 장문 컨텍스트 처리 모델 개발에 중요한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: A Temporal Algebraic Framework for Data Stream Evaluation Under Delayed Labels and Distribution Shifts
items.body: In data streams, labels often arrive late or only for some instances, class prevalence drifts, and rare classes vanish from short windows. Standard evaluation then confuses a degraded decision boundary with a change in prevalence, and is biased when labels are delayed or selected by the model. We extend an algebraic framework that obtains pooled (micro) and per-class (macro) measures from one confusion matrix to streams, weighting the counts in time by exponential fading or a sliding window; the update costs O(m^2) per step, whatever the stream length, and each pooled measure stays a weighted combination of the per-class ones. Delayed and selective feedback enter as an observation mask: until its label arrives, an instance is counted with the model's calibrated class probabilities, and the bias of this interim estimate is driven by their calibration error. Audited conventions report no value for a class without verified instances. We separate prior shift from concept drift by monitoring prior-free coordinates (recall and specificity) and attribute a change in a measure to the two sources with a first-order Jacobian decomposition. On synthetic streams and four real datasets, a detector on these coordinates with a memory per class raises no excess false alarms under label shift, unlike the Jacobian alarm and error-rate detectors. The correction for delayed labels recovers recall in some real settings and is only partial for precision, specificity and F1. Twenty-five statements are checked in Lean 4, and the code is in the aggmetrics package.
items.title_ko: 지연된 라벨 및 분포 변화 환경에서 데이터 스트림 평가를 위한 시간적 대수 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 데이터 스트림에서 라벨 지연, 클래스 불균형, 분포 변화와 같은 문제로 인해 표준 평가 방식이 오작동하는 상황을 해결하기 위한 시간적 대수 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 이 프레임워크는 시간 가중치를 적용하여 단일 혼동 행렬에서 pooled 및 per-class 측정치를 얻어, 라벨 지연이나 모델에 의한 선택 편향을 교정합니다.
items.why_ko: 실시간 데이터 스트림 분석 및 ML 모델 평가의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 필수적인 연구로, 동적인 환경에서 AI 시스템을 안정적으로 운영하려는 개발자에게 유용합니다.

items.title: World-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Pollution-Aware Bird Movement Modeling Using a Multi-Instance DQN Framework
items.body: Birds are modeled as environmentally sensitive agents whose movement reflects real-world air quality conditions, where AQI serves as a measurable world feedback signal representing pollution-driven consequences. Instead of relying on human preference or synthetic rewards, the system uses environmental outcomes as the primary training signal, enabling policy learning grounded in ecological impact. We propose a multi-instance reinforcement learning simulation in which agents navigate a 2D grid representation of India integrated with a precomputed AQI matrix and geographic state boundaries. The framework combines bird call metadata from the Xeno-canto dataset, spatial discretization, and real environmental data to learn adaptive navigation strategies under pollution constraints. To ensure scalability and efficiency, repeated real-time API queries are replaced by a structured AQI mapping that enables fast lookup during training and execution. Multiple baselines, including Monte Carlo, Q-Learning, and Value Iteration, are evaluated for comparison. Deep Q-Network demonstrates stronger stability, adaptability, and cumulative performance across varying environmental conditions, establishing a scalable foundation for world-feedback driven ecological decision modeling.
items.title_ko: 다중 인스턴스 DQN 프레임워크를 이용한 오염 인식 조류 이동 모델링을 위한 월드 기반 강화 학습
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 조류의 이동 패턴을 환경 오염 수준(AQI)에 민감하게 반응하는 에이전트로 모델링하기 위해 월드 기반 강화 학습과 다중 인스턴스 DQN 프레임워크를 사용합니다. 인간 선호도나 합성 보상 대신 실제 환경 결과(오염도)를 학습 신호로 활용하여 생태학적 영향을 기반으로 정책을 학습합니다.
items.why_ko: AI를 활용하여 복잡한 생태학적 현상을 모델링하고 예측하는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하며, 환경 보호 및 기후 변화 연구에 AI를 적용하는 잠재력을 보여줍니다.

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.body:
External sandboxes for coding agents

I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine.

I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects.

My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox.

To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations:

external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly.

external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance.

external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package!

Each of these implementations offers the same localhost API. You can then configure Pi, Claude Code, or Codex to send API calls to that sandbox any time they want to execute code.

The sandboxes also include an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code is allowed to communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent. Here's the UI you can use to reconfigure that proxy while the sandbox is still running:

I continue to be fascinated by the challenge of safely running untrusted code. This external sandbox pattern provides a neat way to experiment with different approaches.

Tags: sandboxing, security, ai, webassembly, generative-ai, llms, coding-agents, claude-code, codex, pi
items.body_ko:
코딩 에이전트를 위한 외부 샌드박스

저는 에이전트가 실행하는 코드를 샌드박스 처리하는 새로운 방법을 탐색해 왔으며, 실수나 프롬프트 인젝션 공격으로 인해 로컬 모델이 기계에 손상을 주는 작업을 수행할 수 있다는 걱정 없이 로컬 모델을 안전하게 시도하는 데 중점을 두었습니다.

저는 Superpowers 및 기타 프로젝트를 개발한 AI 연구소 Prime Radiant와 함께 이 프로젝트를 진행했습니다.

Prime Radiant 블로그에 게시된 제 글은 외부 샌드박스 패턴을 소개합니다. 이 패턴에서는 에이전트가 실행하는 코드가 전용 샌드박스 내에서 실행되는 반면 에이전트 자체는 해당 샌드박스 외부에 존재합니다.

이 패턴을 시연하기 위해 세 가지 샌드박스 서버 구현을 출시했습니다:

external-sandbox-v86은 Node.js 서버를 실행하며, 이 서버는 v86을 사용하여 WebAssembly 내에서 Alpine Linux를 실행합니다.

external-sandbox-container는 Apple Containers 인스턴스 내에서 Alpine Linux로 샌드박스를 실행하는 Python 웹 서버입니다.

external-sandbox-quicksand는 또 다른 Python 웹 서버이며, 이번에는 Microsoft의 Quicksand 샌드박스 라이브러리를 사용합니다. 이 라이브러리는 QEMU와 Alpine Linux를 Python 패키지로 번들링합니다!

각 구현은 동일한 localhost API를 제공합니다. 그런 다음 Pi, Claude Code 또는 Codex를 구성하여 코드를 실행할 때마다 해당 샌드박스로 API 호출을 보낼 수 있습니다.

샌드박스에는 선택적 HTTP/HTTPS 허용 목록 프록시도 포함되어 있어 에이전트 코드가 통신할 수 있는 호스트를 정확하게 제어할 수 있습니다. 또한 에이전트와 비밀을 공유하지 않고도 인증된 API 호출을 수행할 수 있는 자격 증명 대체 메커니즘도 포함되어 있습니다. 샌드박스가 실행 중인 동안 해당 프록시를 재구성하는 데 사용할 수 있는 UI는 다음과 같습니다:

저는 신뢰할 수 없는 코드를 안전하게 실행하는 문제에 계속 매료되어 있습니다. 이 외부 샌드박스 패턴은 다양한 접근 방식을 실험할 수 있는 깔끔한 방법을 제공합니다.

items.title: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol
items.body:
GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol

OpenAI:

We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work.

They're available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. I shipped LLM 0.38 with support for the new models.

6.2 Astra is 80% of the price of 6 Astra - $8/MTok input and $40/MTok output, the same price as Claude Fable 5.2 (which was also 80% of its predecessor). 6 Astra and Fable 5 were both $10/$50. The cached price is an even bigger discount - $0.40/million compared to $1/million for the older model. This is great news for longer running agentic sessions.

GPT-6.2 Sol is the same $2/$10 price as 6.1 Sol and 6 Sol - which are half the price of GPT-5.6 Sol ($4/$20).

Here are the pelicans for GPT-6.2 Sol and for GPT-6.2 Astra. The 6.2 Astra max pelican looks like this:

I have a full comparison grid here, but here's how the high/xhigh/max pelicans compare with the previous Sol and Astra releases:

I also ran my most recent benchmark prompt against the two models, using "Ultra' effort levels in the Codex CLI:

Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data

Here's Sol and here's Astra. Neither of them did a good enough job of morphing Yonkers into a big mech, at least in comparison to Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon.

This video showing the Astra and Sol animations playing out at the same time:

I created that video using GPT-6.2 Astra (Ultra) in the Codex desktop app by prompting:

https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-astra-ultra/index.html and https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-sol-ultra/index.html  are two videos of the same thing by two different models

I need a video of the first 10 seconds where the top half of the video plays the first and the bottom half plays the second

I need an overlaid label of "GPT-6.2 Astra" on the top half and "GPT-6.2 Sol" on the bottom half. These labels should be tastefully positioned.

Make the video square and 2000x2000 pixels

Then later:

OK make it 20s

Here's the exported transcript.

The buzz around these new models is mixed at the moment. Astra 6.2 isn't scoring quite as high as Fable 5.2 on various benchmarks, and I've seen a few complaints that its communication style can be confusing. Theo Browne's review (in the form of a feedback letter he sent OpenAI during pre-release) has this useful example:

When this model is working on long tasks, it can pull in a lot of subagents and manage them pretty well. It will then proceed to randomly ask you some weird internal implementation detail bullshit that you could not under any earthly circumstance understand, much less have input on.

I sent "/goal make a new level for Outer Wilds". 2 hours in, it's "blocked" because it wanted to ask me "does r24's reviewer write it's clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4?"

items.title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide
items.body:
Datasette Lite is my port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide. I've released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it's now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application.

You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL to lite.datasette.io:

Load client-side Datasette to browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script

Select a released version of Datasette to load from PyPI

Load a specific commit, tag, or branch name from the Datasette GitHub repository

Pick from over 100 versions of SQLite to use with Datasette

Install additional Datasette plugins from PyPI or URLs to wheel files, including JavaScript visualization tools

The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo.

As an example, consider the following URL:

https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

Follow that link and, after a short loading screen, you'll find yourself on a page that looks like this:

That's Datasette running the new datasette-maplibre plugin, loading up a database of GeoJSON shapes of countries and displaying both a combined map and individual boundary maps in a table.

Let's break down that URL to see what it's doing:

https://lite.datasette.io/
?install=datasette-maplibre
&url=https://.../demo.db
&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml
#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

The ?install=datasette-maplibre installs that additional plugin from PyPI. You can pass &install=... as many times as you like to load more plugins.

&url=https://.../demo.db loads that SQLite database from the provided URL. These URLs need to have open CORS headers - I host files like this in Gists, because they provide an easy way to get open CORS headers on a web-hosted file.

&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml loads this metadata.yml file. The metadata file adds HTML descriptions to various tables, and to the Datasette homepage. Visit that homepage here for a guided tour of the other features of that plugin, all defined in the metadata file.

#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent is a fragment hash that turns into a location within Datasette - here it's loading the /demo/capitals_and_countries SQL view, then appending another fragment hash to it (%23 is a URL-encoded #) which tells the map plugin to zoom to a certain location and to set the color of the shapes on the map based on the continent column in the data.

That URL is doing a lot of work! I wrote more about this trick for building URL-addressable software in URL-addressable Pyodide Python environments last year.

The full set of supported URL arguments is described in the Datasette Lite README.

I've already started using Datasette Lite as part of the Datasette development process. Here's a recent issue describing a pagination bug - I posted a comment there demonstrating the old, broken behavior and the new fix using links to Datasette Lite:

Demo of the bug: https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a42&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score - click next and the second page is empty.

Here's that same page with the bug fixed (running on 1.0a43): https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a43&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score

How this works, using service workers

Datasette Lite is not a new project. I launched the first version back in 2022, originally as a bit of a joke (running server-side apps in the browser is pretty funny) but one that quickly started proving its value.

The problem with that initial version is that it was a hack. It worked by running Datasette in a Pyodide web worker, simulating requests through that stack, then injecting the resulting HTML back into the top level page using innerHTML.

This worked for basic Datasette, but meant that any feature that used JavaScript failed to work, because script tags in innerHTML don't execute, and the web worker tricks it used failed to load additional JavaScript or CSS files.

The new version takes a completely different approach based on Service Workers. These allow JavaScript to intercept HTTP requests for new pages and resources and serve them from client-side code instead.

Datasette Lite registers a service worker for the entire lite.datasette.io domain. The parent page then creates an iframe that sends requests for Datasette pages to URLs that look like this:

/app/aa94e6851595/ # the homepage (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/data/places # a table page (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/navigation-search.js # (JavaScript)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/app.css # (CSS)

Those are regular Datasette URLs, but with a /app/aa94e6851595/ prefix. What's that about?

The /app/<session>/ prefix is necessary because of multiple tabs.

Consider the URL above, which loads the demo instance with the datasette-maplibre plugin. That URL defines a full, custom Datasette instance. You might have that one running in a tab, then one of my other demo links running in another.

The service worker for lite.datasette.io is shared between all of those tabs. If it routed to a single instance of Datasette then every tab would share that underlying instance, no matter what plugins or other settings their URL attempted to configure.

Instead, the parent page generates a random session ID and uses it as a prefix for all of the subsequent hidden asset and page loads. The service worker can then use that session ID to route those requests back through the parent page to a web worker running a dedicated Datasette instance for that particular session.

(We still need a web worker because Pyodide in a service worker would not be able to maintain state beyond around 30 seconds, depending on the browser. There are a lot of moving parts here!)

I had Claude Fable 5.2 generate several SVG diagrams to help explain this. Here's my favorite of those, now embedded in the Datasette Lite README:

This system started life back in May as an AI research spike generated using Claude Opus 4.8. It wasn't until November (and Claude Fable 5.2) that I felt familiar enough with how it all works to confidently ship it to production!

Bonus feature: pick your version of SQLite

I added this feature last night as an off-shoot of investigating a potential bug in SQLite.

Datasette is meant to work against any released version of SQLite since 3.25 (released in September 2018). There have been 87 further releases since then.

Being able to fire up Datasette against a specific version of SQLite is really useful for demonstrating new SQLite features and debugging weird issues.

In the past I've used various tricks to get different SQLite versions running with Python on my Mac, but it's not a trivial process.

WebAssembly is perfect for this. I can load up a custom SQLite build entirely in my browser, test it there, then discard it when I close my tab.

datasette/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels is my new repository which contains WebAssembly compiled Python wheels for pysqlite3 for 163 different SQLite versions. Each version gets a file with a name like this:

pysqlite3-0.6.2-3.54.1-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl

That's for SQLite 3.54.1, the most recent version.

Datasette Lite now takes a special ?sqlite= URL parameter, which will accept a version number like 3.54.1, resolve the path to the corresponding wheel file,
items.body_ko:
Datasette Lite는 Datasette Python 애플리케이션을 WebAssembly 및 Pyodide를 사용하여 브라우저에서 직접 실행하도록 포팅한 것입니다. 서비스 워커를 사용하여 Datasette Lite를 완전히 다시 작성했으며, 이제 실제 서버 측 애플리케이션과 거의 구별할 수 없습니다.

이제 lite.datasette.io에 신중하게 제작된 URL을 사용하여 다음 모든 작업을 수행할 수 있습니다:

클라이언트 측 Datasette를 로드하여 모든 SQLite 데이터베이스, JSON 파일, CSV 파일 또는 SQL 스크립트를 탐색합니다.

PyPI에서 로드할 Datasette의 릴리스 버전을 선택합니다.

Datasette GitHub 저장소에서 특정 커밋, 태그 또는 브랜치 이름을 로드합니다.

Datasette와 함께 사용할 100가지 이상의 SQLite 버전 중에서 선택합니다.

JavaScript 시각화 도구를 포함하여 PyPI 또는 휠 파일 URL에서 추가 Datasette 플러그인을 설치합니다.

특정 Datasette 참조, 플러그인 및 SQLite 버전을 로드하는 기능은 진행 중인 기능 또는 버그 재현의 데모를 링크하는 데 환상적인 도구입니다. 이 데모를 제공하기 위해 전체 웹 서버를 가동할 필요가 없습니다.

예를 들어 다음 URL을 고려해 보겠습니다:

https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

이 링크를 따라가면 짧은 로딩 화면 후에 다음과 같은 페이지를 보게 될 것입니다:

이것은 새로운 datasette-maplibre 플러그인을 실행하는 Datasette이며, 국가의 GeoJSON 모양 데이터베이스를 로드하고 결합된 맵과 개별 경계 맵을 테이블에 표시합니다.

이 URL이 무엇을 하는지 분석해 봅시다:

https://lite.datasette.io/
?install=datasette-maplibre
&url=https://.../demo.db
&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml
#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

?install=datasette-maplibre는 PyPI에서 추가 플러그인을 설치합니다. 더 많은 플러그인을 로드하기 위해 &install=...을 여러 번 전달할 수 있습니다.

&url=https://.../demo.db는 제공된 URL에서 SQLite 데이터베이스를 로드합니다. 이러한 URL에는 공개 CORS 헤더가 필요합니다. 저는 Gist에 이와 같은 파일을 호스팅합니다. 이는 웹 호스팅 파일에 공개 CORS 헤더를 쉽게 얻을 수 있는 방법을 제공하기 때문입니다.

&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml은 이 metadata.yml 파일을 로드합니다. 메타데이터 파일은 다양한 테이블과 Datasette 홈페이지에 HTML 설명을 추가합니다. 이 홈페이지를 방문하여 메타데이터 파일에 정의된 플러그인의 다른 기능을 안내받으세요.

#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent는 Datasette 내의 위치로 바뀌는 프래그먼트 해시입니다. 여기서는 /demo/capitals_and_countries SQL 뷰를 로드한 다음, 다른 프래그먼트 해시(%23는 URL 인코딩된 #)를 추가하여 맵 플러그인에 특정 위치로 확대하고 데이터의 continent 열을 기반으로 맵의 도형 색상을 설정하도록 지시합니다.

이 URL은 많은 작업을 수행하고 있습니다! 작년에 URL-addressable Pyodide Python environments에서 URL-addressable 소프트웨어를 구축하는 이 트릭에 대해 더 많이 썼습니다.

지원되는 URL 인수의 전체 세트는 Datasette Lite README에 설명되어 있습니다.

저는 이미 Datasette Lite를 Datasette 개발 프로세스의 일부로 사용하기 시작했습니다. 다음은 페이지네이션 버그를 설명하는 최근 이슈입니다. 저는 Datasette Lite 링크를 사용하여 이전의 깨진 동작과 새로운 수정 사항을 시연하는 댓글을 게시했습니다:

버그 데모: https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a42&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score - 다음을 클릭하면 두 번째 페이지가 비어 있습니다.

버그가 수정된 동일한 페이지 (1.0a43에서 실행): https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a43&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score

서비스 워커를 사용한 작동 방식

Datasette Lite는 새로운 프로젝트가 아닙니다. 2022년에 처음 버전을 출시했습니다. 처음에는 농담처럼 (브라우저에서 서버 측 앱을 실행하는 것은 꽤 재미있습니다) 시작했지만, 빠르게 그 가치를 증명하기 시작했습니다.

초기 버전의 문제는 해킹이었다는 것입니다. Datasette를 Pyodide 웹 워커에서 실행하고, 해당 스택을 통해 요청을 시뮬레이션한 다음, innerHTML을 사용하여 결과 HTML을 최상위 페이지에 다시 주입하는 방식으로 작동했습니다.

이것은 기본적인 Datasette에서는 작동했지만, JavaScript를 사용하는 모든 기능이 작동하지 않았습니다. innerHTML의 스크립트 태그는 실행되지 않고, 웹 워커 트릭은 추가 JavaScript 또는 CSS 파일을 로드하지 못했기 때문입니다.

새로운 버전은 서비스 워커를 기반으로 완전히 다른 접근 방식을 취합니다. 이를 통해 JavaScript는 새 페이지 및 리소스에 대한 HTTP 요청을 가로채고 클라이언트 측 코드에서 제공할 수 있습니다.

Datasette Lite는 전체 lite.datasette.io 도메인에 대한 서비스 워커를 등록합니다. 그런 다음 부모 페이지는 다음과 같은 Datasette 페이지에 대한 요청을 보내는 iframe을 생성합니다:

/app/aa94e6851595/ # 홈페이지 (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/data/places # 테이블 페이지 (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/navigation-search.js # (JavaScript)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/app.css # (CSS)

이들은 일반적인 Datasette URL이지만, /app/aa94e6851595/ 접두사가 붙습니다. 이것은 무엇일까요?

/app/<session>/ 접두사는 여러 탭 때문에 필요합니다.

datasette-maplibre 플러그인과 함께 데모 인스턴스를 로드하는 위 URL을 고려해 보십시오. 이 URL은 완전한 사용자 지정 Datasette 인스턴스를 정의합니다. 한 탭에서 이 인스턴스를 실행하고, 다른 탭에서 다른 데모 링크를 실행할 수 있습니다.

lite.datasette.io에 대한 서비스 워커는 이러한 모든 탭 간에 공유됩니다. 단일 Datasette 인스턴스로 라우팅되면 모든 탭이 해당 기본 인스턴스를 공유하게 되며, URL이 구성하려고 시도한 플러그인이나 다른 설정과는 상관없이 공유됩니다.

대신, 부모 페이지는 무작위 세션 ID를 생성하고 모든 요청에 대한 접두사로 사용합니다.

items.title: Cloudflare Joins the Jevolution and Labels Itself a Neolab
items.body:
Cloudflare has been one of the essential infrastructure companies of the web for the past decade and a half. But now, it’s turning into a neolab — at least according to a presentation at AI Engineer Code Summit by Michelle Chen, who runs Cloudflare’s AI Platform on the product side.

We’ll get into what exactly a neolab is in a minute (the short version: they build models and they’re not called OpenAI or Anthropic). Cloudflare is claiming to be one because it too has begun to launch models. Two System One models, to be precise: Clef and Clairic. As Chen explained in her talk, Clef is a decision model directly inspired by TypeSafe AI’s revolutionary Jev model, while Clairic is a new type of system one model that Cloudflare calls an “extract” model.

In an interview with Latent Space after her presentation, Chen hinted that Cloudflare won’t just be producing system one models. There will be large language models, too.

“We're not being a neolab [to] only launch system one models, even though it makes sense for our infrastructure. We've kind of entered this Pandora's box now, right? We opened it, now the possibilities are endless.”

Chen said it’s “not just system one models, but potentially reasoning models that we've been experimenting with, and other LLMs and whatnot.”

However, she added that these probably won’t be pre-trained models built from scratch, like the frontier labs produce.

“I don't think that's our focus, but I think we can take existing resources out there and make [them] a lot more efficient and effective.”

She noted that “most of our team really just does post-training,” so that will be the focus in model development.

What is a neolab and is Cloudflare really one?

The term neolab literally means a ‘new lab’ and it was coined last November by Stephanie Palazzolo from The Information, who defined it as “a new generation of research-focused AI startups.”

Deedy Das, a partner at Menlo Ventures and an AI influencer, runs a big list of neolabs. It includes companies like Thinking Machines Lab, Poolside, and TypeSafe AI itself. According to Das, neolabs employ elite researchers, spend a lot of compute (“usually to train its own AI model”), don't have significant revenue traction, and they’re typically startups that have raised a lot of money.

Deedy Das’ list of neolabs — note that TypeSafe is among the top 20.

Cloudflare doesn’t tick at least half of those boxes, since it’s a public company with significant revenue traction. In fact, earlier this month Cloudflare announced record earnings. “The third quarter was Cloudflare's best quarter ever,” said CEO Matthew Prince. “We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue with revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year.”

So Cloudflare as a “neolab” is pushing the accepted definition. However, as Chen argued in her presentation, building models is part of a natural progression for the company: from infrastructure, to compute (e.g. the Workers platform, including now for agents), to storage, to serving open weight models like Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek (on Workers AI), to now building its own models.

Jev as the “east wind”

Chen readily admits that Jev inspired Cloudflare’s pivot to building models. Referencing a Chinese proverb, she framed Jev’s arrival in September as “the east wind” that unexpectedly changed how Cloudflare viewed AI models.

“And so when the system one and Jev paradigm started coming on board,” Chen said in her presentation, “we were like, this makes so much sense for us to adopt, right? We don't have to send every request to an LLM. We can send some of it to a System One model.”

In our conversation, Chen commented on how it took only two weeks for them to build Clef — which is a copy of Jev — whereas it took TypeSafe AI two years to build Jev. She meant that as a compliment for how hard TypeSafe AI worked to create this new type of model.

“All credit to TypeSafe, really, for actually attacking this space and inventing something new here, that people could relate to so strongly and be able to use it. And, yeah, we came up with a model super quickly, but they put in a lot of legwork and we knew exactly what the API schema should look like and whatnot.”

Cloudflare is, at its core, still an infrastructure company — speed and low latency is its meat and potatoes. The main benefit of System One models, Chen remarked, is that they allow more work to be done by smaller, faster models, where output is measured in milliseconds rather than seconds.

Clairic and what extraction models do

While Clef was a clone of Jev, Cloudflare soon came up with an original twist on System One with Clairic, launched last month as “the first model in a new class: System One extraction models.”

“What Clairic does is it can take unstructured input, and it can extract, compute, estimate and forecast values from those inputs,” Chen explained in her presentation.

In our interview, Chen said that her team wanted to use System One principles to find other areas where LLMs were “overkill” and didn’t always return the right answer.

One of the problems they settled on was that LLMs don’t always deal well with unstructured input. Because LLMs are autoregressive, Chen explained, they are prone to hallucinate and they sometimes return malformed JSON.

“So we used the same System One principles [as Jev/Clef] there, and decided on extraction.”

Some examples of system one use cases at Cloudflare.

She used the example of an invoice, where an LLM will sometimes get an important detail wrong — like the order number.

“When you send it [the order] to an LLM, they're like, wait, I think the order number's three, maybe it's four, maybe it's five. But it's like, the number's right there, you just have to read it!”

So the idea with Clairic is that it will extract a typed value — like a number — from unstructured data, in one forward pass.

Why Cloudflare is in the lab now

Using the label “neolab” sounds a bit like a marketing gimmick, but it also makes a ton of sense for Cloudflare to produce system one models — and even, in future, reasoning models.

“Being a neolab means that we can create what we are missing,” Chen said in her presentation.

In our interview, she also mentioned that creating their own models allows Cloudflare to derisk its AI operations.

“I think there's a lot of risk in the AI space, because just like Jev was closed source and we couldn't run it, there [are] a lot of models out there [with] maybe regulatory risks coming up, like the Chinese open source models. I think lots of model labs want to actually make money, as well — so enforcing quite expensive licenses.”

If you look at Cloudflare’s product page now, it resembles what Amazon’s cloud computing product page looked like at the height of Web 2.0 — i.e. there’s a lot there!

But there’s still room for several more models.

items.title: [AINews] Perplexity hits a $1B revenue run rate, up 4x in 2026
items.body:
Perplexity crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate today, CEO Aravind Srinivas told Semafor at a live event. The Information reported previously under $250M at the start of the year and over $750M by August, with Computer driving some of the growth. At usual agent lab multiples (eg Cognition also crossed $1B, with Cursor crossing $4.6B), this would roughly mean that Perplexity is now worth $30-50B — if the unit economics hold up. This is a nice bump on the $20B round in September 2025, and qualifies for our “>$10B fundraise” rule for title stories.

Gathering up some recent Perplexity launches for those catching up:

Computer. September’s Automations let it pick up recurring tasks where it left off. November’s Teammates take on ongoing jobs. Computer also runs fully locally on supported Macs.

Monitor API. Watch a topic or page and get a webhook when something relevant changes.

Frontier Research. The new research lab has access to 10,000+ GPUs and plans to publish papers, data, models, and code.

Sponsored by Deepgram
Deepgram is the voice AI infrastructure behind natural conversation—bringing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice-focused LLMs, and agents to teams building with voice AI. For any stack and any tools you already love building with, Deepgram slots in as your foundational voice AI technology. So you have control. And we have the context to listen, understand, and speak like a human.
Learn more about the Real-time Context Standard.

AI Twitter Recap

Qwen4-Max in the wild

Friday’s Qwen4-Max preview is now a shipping model. At the highest reasoning setting, Qwen4-Max scored 43 on the Intelligence Index, up from 34. Average cost fell from $10.02 to $3.27 per task. Alibaba cut output pricing from $6 to $4.50 per million tokens, and the model generated about 39% fewer of them. Kimi K3.1 Pro cost $3.68 per index task and scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to Qwen’s 48%. Artificial Analysis

Inside the model. Alibaba kept the total parameter count at 2.4T and reduced the number active per token by 25% to 71B. The model takes images and text, with a 1M-token context window. Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are still to come. Alibaba

Arena and Vals: Arena ranks it #14 overall on Agent Arena, the top Chinese model, with +7.5% net over 14.7k sessions (Arena).
WebDev: It placed #6 in Code Arena WebDev at 1750, +74 over its predecessor (WebDev). It also placed #6 in Image-to-WebDev, just above Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol (I2WebDev).

Vals Index: It is #11 overall, with large gains in coding and finance (Vals).

Legal-benchmark caveat: On HLAB it gets 95.7% of checklist items right but passes only 21.3% of tasks, and its output tokens rise 3.6x (HLAB).

Vision results (independent): Roboflow calls it underwhelming on its VLM benchmark, with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic now far ahead. At high reasoning effort, however, it is ~4.5x faster and ~68% cheaper per image than Qwen3.8-Max (Roboflow).

Safety, alignment and eval integrity

OpenAI embedded assessments: OpenAI is giving Apollo, METR, Transluce and Goodfire internal access to its models and systems (OpenAI).
Scope by group: Apollo places six evaluators onsite for four months (Rundown). METR reviews OpenAI's largest RL run, with access to transcripts, monitor records and checkpoint snapshots (METR). Transluce runs a six-week audit of post-training alignment evals, with a fuller follow-up in early 2027 (Transluce). Goodfire embeds interpretability researchers to monitor training runs (Goodfire).

Limits: METR says its scope excludes the misalignment incidents OpenAI has disclosed and is narrower than METR proposed (scope).

Criticism of the access terms: Critics say the deals fall short of Sam Altman's promise of "employee-like access."
Reported gaps: Assessors get no Slack access, OpenAI selects which staff they interview, and they cannot access weights or run training-based elicitation (Neel Nanda, Alex Mallen).

Former-employee account: Mikita Balesni says assessors cannot quote employees, even anonymously, and some may be barred from publishing on internal-only models (balesni).

Goodfire acquisition talks: The Information reports OpenAI explored buying the interpretability startup for more than $5B. Goodfire reportedly wanted to stay independent so it could sell to multiple labs (report).

Other integrity signals:
Benchmark contamination: Claude appears to have memorized details of the LinuxArena control eval (Karvonen).

Incident taxonomy: OpenAI published a v0.1 framework for classifying AI control incidents (framework).

Disclosure policy: Anthropic is cutting its coordinated disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities (policy).

Inference systems and agent infrastructure

Together moves on from hand-tuned megakernels. Its first design made it into production for one customer. Agents now search for smaller groups of GPU operations to fuse. Together reports 28% higher throughput on Llama 3.2 1B on B200. Engineering writeup

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Vera Rubin: vLLM with Dynamo on SemiAnalysis's AgentX benchmark shows 63.4x per-chip throughput over GB300 NVL72 at 400 tok/s/user, and 93.3x at 600 (vLLM).
Batch-1 latency: SGLang-adjacent work reaches ~2,500 tok/s at batch size 1 on TP4, 1.7x its GB300 result (saltyph). Baseten reports a similar 1.7x over its 4xB300 numbers (Baseten).

Agent-driven optimization: An agent shared Engram tables across HBM via NVLink symmetric memory to recover prefix-cache capacity (Liu). Another team says agents found optimizations that made its B300 step time 10% faster (Halex).

Agentic serving research: MIT's Evolving Infra replaces fixed prefill/decode disaggregation with online adaptation. Against NVIDIA Dynamo on up to 256 GB300s, it reports up to 4.1x lower latency and 14x lower P95 TTFT (Evolving Infra).
Pipeline-parallel prefill: Inferact finds PP2 on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash sustains 23% more requests per GPU than DEP2 at a 2s TTFT target (Inferact).

Prefix-cache pitfalls: Ollama found that a single system-prompt timestamp or a change in reasoning effort can wipe the cache (Ollama).

Sandboxes and training:
External sandboxes: Simon Willison describes running agents on a Mac while executing their code in WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandboxes. The pattern includes allow-list proxies and credential replacement (post).

MLPerf: In MLPerf Training v6.1, a GB300 NVL72 trained GPT-OSS-20B in 19.7 minutes, 2.86x faster than H100 (Lambda).

One endpoint for open models. Hugging Face Inference Providers now runs on OpenRouter using the same endpoint and token. Hugging Face

Research, benchmarks and evals

PyBot: A swarm of 1,000 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agents spent a week writing a rule-based chatbot with no neural network (lewtun).
Scale: The agents exchanged ~175k messages and merged ~8k PRs.

Result: The bot is 630k lines of Python with zero dependencies and is reported on par with SmolLM-360M on everyday questions.

Self-improvement and training:
AutoRL: Agents supervising a live RL run lifted Qwen3 on AIME 2024 from 46.67% to 66.67% (omarsar0).

Benchmark-gaming caveat: A roundup warns that many self-improving agent gains come from learning the benchmark rather than the task (TuringPost).

Weight-space programming: Opus 5.5 hand-wrote transformer weights that solved algorithmic tasks with a median of 166 parameters (dair_ai).

Data curation: DatologyAI published the tech report behind its claimed 6x pretraining compute multiplier (Datology).

Distillation reproduction: A small-scale replication confirms perturbed-input distillation helps when the student trains from scratch, but finds it hurts when distilling into a pretrained student (Maini).

New benchmarks:
GradeBench: The best frontier model agrees with instructors only 57% of the time when grading handwritten physics answers (GradeBench).

Time to First Audio: AA's new TTS latency benchmark finds a median of 376 ms for streaming models versus 2.0 s for non-streamin

items.title: Nathan Lambert: Everyone online: OMG Qwen 4 Max is closed source, Chinese open-weight strategy is over.
items.body:
Everyone online: OMG Qwen 4 Max is closed source, Chinese open-weight strategy is over.

In reality: It's the same strategy they've had for years. Qwen keeps the strongest model API only and has an abundant open weight strategy below that.

items.why_ko: 개발 커뮤니티에서 활발히 논의되는 웹어셈블리 기반 클라이언트 사이드 파이썬 앱의 실제 구현 사례를 보여주며, 프런트엔드와 백엔드 개발의 경계를 허무는 기술적 진보를 보여줍니다.

items.title: PyTorch: How can a shared software stack help bring PyTorch support to new chips? At #PyTorchCon North Americ
items.body:
How can a shared software stack help bring PyTorch support to new chips? At #PyTorchCon North America 2026, Chris Lattner (Qualcomm) explains the approach behind MAX and Mojo, drawing on the history of GCC and LLVM.

Watch the full keynote: https://youtu.be/2XXf_iL1WhA?si=avH-JniejXLnHC0i
items.title_ko: PyTorch, 공유 소프트웨어 스택으로 새로운 칩 지원 확장
items.summary_ko: Chris Lattner (Qualcomm)가 #PyTorchCon North America 2026에서 PyTorch가 새로운 칩을 지원할 수 있도록 돕는 공유 소프트웨어 스택의 중요성에 대해 설명했습니다. GCC와 LLVM의 역사를 예로 들어 MAX와 Mojo의 접근 방식을 소개하며, 하드웨어 확장을 위한 소프트웨어 인프라의 역할을 강조합니다.
items.why_ko: PyTorch가 더 다양한 하드웨어에서 효율적으로 작동하도록 하는 핵심 전략을 제시하며, 이는 AI 모델의 배포 및 활용 범위를 넓히는 데 중요한 역할을 합니다.

items.title: PyTorch: Developers can post-train Meta’s Muse Spark Open with NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel, a PyTorch native librar
items.body:
Developers can post-train Meta’s Muse Spark Open with NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel, a PyTorch native library supporting full SFT and LoRA fine tuning without model conversion.

https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/scale-agentic-coding-workflows-with-metas-muse-spark-open-on-nvidia-gb300-nvl72/
items.title_ko: Meta Muse Spark Open, NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel로 후속 훈련 가능
items.summary_ko: 개발자들이 Meta의 Muse Spark Open 모델을 NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel을 사용하여 후속 훈련할 수 있게 되었습니다. NeMo AutoModel은 PyTorch 네이티브 라이브러리로, 모델 변환 없이 전체 SFT(Supervised Fine-Tuning) 및 LoRA 파인 튜닝을 지원합니다.
items.why_ko: 개발자들이 Meta의 오픈 모델을 NVIDIA 스택에서 쉽게 파인튜닝하고 활용할 수 있게 되어, 에이전트 코딩 워크플로우를 확장하고 모델 커스터마이징을 용이하게 합니다.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: A rush of patches to address security concerns is exactly the most plausible answer for recent outag
items.body: A rush of patches to address security concerns is exactly the most plausible answer for recent outages, as well as the official answer. CIOs I spoke to have been exhausted trying to keep up with security patch demands & balancing that with normal operations. www.washingtonsun.com/technology/b...
items.title_ko: 최근 서비스 중단은 보안 패치 러시 때문일 가능성 높아
items.summary_ko: 최근 발생한 서비스 중단 사태의 가장 타당한 원인은 보안 우려를 해결하기 위한 긴급 패치 적용일 가능성이 높다고 Ethan Mollick이 언급했습니다. CIO들은 보안 패치 요구사항과 운영 균형을 맞추는 데 어려움을 겪고 있다고 덧붙였습니다.
items.why_ko: AI 서비스 운영의 복잡성과 보안의 중요성을 상기시키며, 안정적인 서비스 제공을 위한 보안 패치 관리의 어려움을 개발자 관점에서 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: I’ve been using GPT-6.2 Astra prior to launch & I found it very uneven  & weird. On one hand, it was
items.body: I’ve been using GPT-6.2 Astra prior to launch & I found it very uneven  & weird. On one hand, it was harder to steer & work with than other models. On the other, when given an ambitious project (make a space elevator from scratch with Blender & Unity) it delivers upwell-tetherline.netlify.app/unity/
items.body_ko: 저는 출시 전에 GPT-6.2 Astra를 사용했는데, 매우 고르지 못하고 이상하다는 것을 알았습니다. 한편으로는 다른 모델보다 조종하고 작업하기가 더 어려웠습니다. 다른 한편으로는 야심찬 프로젝트(Blender와 Unity로 처음부터 우주 엘리베이터 만들기)를 받았을 때 upwell-tetherline.netlify.app/unity/를 제공합니다.
items.title_ko: Ethan Mollick: GPT-6.2 Astra 사용 경험 - 고르지 않고 기묘하지만 야심찬 프로젝트에서는 강력
items.summary_ko: Ethan Mollick이 GPT-6.2 Astra 출시 전 사용 경험을 공유했습니다. 모델이 일관성이 없고 다루기 어렵다고 느꼈지만, Blender와 Unity로 '우주 엘리베이터'를 만드는 것과 같은 야심찬 프로젝트에서는 놀라운 결과물을 내놓았다고 평가했습니다.
items.why_ko: 새로운 최고 성능 모델에 대한 실제 개발자의 사용 후기로, 모델의 강점과 약점을 파악하고 특정 작업에 활용하는 데 실질적인 가이드라인을 제공합니다.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: The discussion of AI in gaming is pernicious now. The idea that games are going to be the only field
items.body: The discussion of AI in gaming is pernicious now. The idea that games are going to be the only field where humans write code unassisted is obviously wrong. But the push for that from press & fans means missing a chance to guide AI usage toward approaches that empower workers & help gaming thrive.
items.title_ko: AI 게임 논의: 개발자 권한 강화에 초점 맞춰야
items.summary_ko: Ethan Mollick은 AI가 게임 분야에서 인간 개발자의 코딩을 완전히 대체할 것이라는 논의가 유해하다고 비판합니다. 대신, AI 활용을 통해 개발자의 역량을 강화하고 게임 산업이 번성할 수 있는 방향으로 논의를 이끌어가야 한다고 주장합니다.
items.why_ko: AI가 게임 개발에 미치는 영향을 균형 잡힌 시각으로 바라보고, 개발자들이 AI를 도구로 활용하여 창의성을 극대화할 수 있는 방향을 모색하는 데 중요한 관점을 제시합니다.

At the top of Nvidia’s earnings call Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

items.title_ko: 엔비디아 이사회, 젠슨 황 CEO 사임 만장일치 수락
items.summary_ko: 엔비디아의 새로운 이사회 의장인 Harvey Jones가 화요일 실적 발표 콜에서 '엔비디아 이사회는 젠슨 황 CEO의 사임을 만장일치로 수락했으며, 젠슨 황을 CEO로 재선임할 의사가 없다'고 발표했습니다. 그의 퇴임에 대한 추가 질문은 받지 않겠다고 밝혔습니다.
items.why_ko: 젠슨 황은 엔비디아의 AI 반도체 성공을 이끈 상징적인 인물로, 그의 사임은 AI 하드웨어 업계와 엔비디아의 미래 전략에 엄청난 파급 효과를 가져올 중대한 소식입니다.

items.title: Hayden Field: Hours before Nvidia's earnings call, Jensen Huang makes a public statement:
items.body:
Hours before Nvidia's earnings call, Jensen Huang makes a public statement: 

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
items.title_ko: 젠슨 황, 엔비디아 이사회에 CEO 복귀 의사 표명
items.summary_ko: 엔비디아 실적 발표 콜 몇 시간 전, 젠슨 황은 공개 성명을 통해 '이사회에서 자신의 복귀가 주주, 직원, 회사, 그리고 미국의 이익에 부합한다고 결정한다면, CEO로 복귀하는 것을 영광으로 생각할 것'이라고 밝혔습니다. 이는 이사회 결정에 대한 그의 의지를 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: 이 소식은 젠슨 황의 사임과 맞물려 엔비디아의 리더십 공백과 향후 경영 방향에 대한 불확실성을 증폭시키는 동시에, AI 업계 전체에 큰 영향을 미칠 수 있는 매우 중요한 사건입니다.
